correctness.rationale: Newton identities and the order-three recurrence prove all cases over Z/p^k. When p≥5, invertibility of 2 and 3 fixes all elementary symmetric coefficients. At 2^k, the ambiguity t in E2 satisfies 2t=0 and induces only even factors, vanishing for all further moments. At 3^k, 3t=et=tP2=0; every later power sum mod 3 is one of p1,p2, so induction proves the five-moment cutoff. Hensel-lifted roots of X^3-X+3^(k-1) give matching four moments and differing fifth moments. Elementary local witnesses and CRT establish sharpness for every N. Exact finite enumeration and witness tests corroborated the statement without replacing proof.

value.rationale: The minimal prefix of modular moments that determines every later moment is a natural sharp invariant in local power-sum systems, motivated by Vinogradov systems and modular Newton identities. This complete classification for three entries shows a surprising discontinuity at a square factor 9 and proves that a fifth moment can contain information not present in the first four; a nontrivial Hensel-lifted cubic construction demonstrates an exact boundary. This is not a textbook single substitution or an arbitrary finite modulus cutoff.
